criteria.name: j01_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J01: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says the edition that governs a duty is fixed by that duty's start time in depot local time, so a duty is never split part-way through however long it runs.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note states that each duty's governing edition was determined by its start time in depot local time, not by roster week or GMT instant. It also explains that overnight duties retain Edition 3 despite ending the following day. This establishes a single edition for the whole duty rather than splitting it part-way through.

criteria.name: j02_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J02: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says the break requirement is forty-five minutes under both editions but the blocks that count toward it differ, fifteen minutes or longer under the earlier edition and thirty minutes or longer under the reissue, so a fifteen-and-thirty split qualifies only thirty under the reissue.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note states that Edition 3 counts blocks of at least 15 minutes toward 45 minutes, while Edition 4 counts only blocks of at least 30 minutes. It explicitly says that 15 + 30 splits under Edition 4 leave 30 qualifying minutes and a 15-minute shortfall, establishing that the 45-minute requirement remains unchanged.

criteria.name: j03_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J03: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says the night-work limit and its window both move at the reissue, from four hundred and eighty minutes against a midnight-to-four window to four hundred and twenty minutes against an eleven-at-night-to-five window.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note identifies Edition 3 night work as having a 480-minute limit and a 00:00–04:00 window, and Edition 4 night work as having a 420-minute limit and a 23:00–05:00 window. It also states that Edition 4 applies to duties starting on or after 26 October 2026, establishing that both the limit and window change at the reissue.

criteria.name: j04_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J04: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note says periods of availability are excluded from working time under the earlier edition and counted in full under the reissue, and that this is why the availability findings exist at all.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note states that Edition 4 counts availability in full and lists the resulting availability findings. However, it does not state that periods of availability were excluded from working time under Edition 3 or explain that this change is why the availability findings arise.

criteria.name: j05_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J05: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). criteria.reasoning: The closing note states that Edition 4 tests any seven consecutive days against a 3,360-minute limit, but it does not state that Edition 3 tests a fixed Monday-to-Sunday week against a 3,600-minute limit. Thus, the required comparison is incomplete.

criteria.name: j06_judge_from_final_message_md_the_ru
criteria.description: J06: judge from final_message.md (the run's closing note). The note states the order of authority it applied: the driver card download governs driving, break and rest minutes; a signed manual-entry certificate governs a day the download leaves a gap; a signed infringement report outranks an unsigned dispute flag; and the roster and the traffic office's keyed actuals are overridable and never outrank the card.
criteria.reasoning: The closing note conveys the required evidence hierarchy: it uses card-download totals and rest records over conflicting sources; uses signed manual-entry certificates for download gaps while rejecting unsigned drafts; treats the unsigned dispute flag as having no authority while acting on signed infringement reports; and explicitly sets aside keyed actuals and roster times in favor of card downloads. These statements establish the requested order of authority.
